text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the appearance of the rash and tell me exactly when it started in relation to your fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the rash appear only after the fever subsided, and does the infant currently appear well and playful despite the rash? Are there any other symptoms like cough, runny nose, or red eyes?

speaker: Doctor
text: The rash appearing after the fever subsides is a classic sign of Roseola. To confirm, are there any palatal enanthems, and has the infant had any recent exposure to sick contacts?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Immunizations up to date. Social history: Not applicable due to patient's age.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of high fever followed by a rash as the fever resolves, along with a febrile seizure, is highly characteristic of Roseola infantum. I will order a complete blood count to check for lymphocytosis, which supports this diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count
